subject: science
prompt:
# How Would You Even Know?

Everything so far has been an argument about things nobody had ever seen. Cells are far too small for human eyes.

> **What is actually stopping you from seeing one?**

Commit to an answer. The rest of the lesson tests it.

options.text: Cells are transparent, so there is nothing to see.
options.feedback: Transparency is a genuine nuisance and there are stains for it. But something else is the hard limit.

options.text: They are smaller than the eye can separate, so a way of magnifying them was needed.
They move too fast to follow.
options.feedback: Some do move. Speed is not what keeps them invisible.

options.text: They are hidden inside larger structures.
options.feedback: Peel a leaf apart and the cells are right there on the surface, still invisible.
